model.architecture: InternVL3-1B is the smallest InternVL3 vision-language model: an InternViT vision encoder + pixel-shuffle + MLP projector feeding a Qwen2.5-0.5B language decoder.

variants.quantization: Decoder Qwen2.5-0.5B int4 weights (symmetric, blockwise-32 + OCTAV), input embedding INT8 (externalized); vision encoder + pixel-shuffle + MLP projector int8; integer compute

recommended.reason: measured on one Galaxy S26 with one binary: GPU 84.41 tok/s decode / 1250.8 prefill, peak 443 MB, init 1.4 s (S4 GPU gate 2026-08-25, 1 run) against CPU 73.76-81.7 decode / 299.4-358.7 prefill, peak 603 MB, init 1.0 s (S7 Android backfill 2026-09-05, 2 cold runs). Same-device CPU control taken: decode is a wash (within 10%); gpu is kept for its prefill advantage (time to first token), a deliberate choice rather than a decode win
card: Use the CPU backend on the desktop.

platform_notes: Accuracy note: output is coherent and image-grounded (CPU-verified). The GPU single-image claim is stated by analogy — 'On-device behavior mirrors the larger InternVL3-2B build (same conversion recipe)' — not as a measurement of this file.
Vision-only bundle (no audio tower): load with the image (vision) tower enabled, modalities Modality.textImage / [.vision].
Galaxy S26 GPU gate prompt carries no image: it covers engine creation and the text path only; the vision path on the GPU is not measured there.
Galaxy S26 GPU gate: XNNPACK additionally takes 1 of the 4 nodes in `main`; the runtime accepts that split.
2026-08-28 start_token fix (metadata-only, weights unchanged): the literal start token "None" was removed. Accuracy figures on the card were measured on the previous file and not re-measured.

2026-08-29 default system prompt restored (metadata-only, weights unchanged): with no system message the prompt now adds 37 prefill tokens, so time-to-first-token grows by that much; per-token speed is unchanged. Accuracy figures not re-measured.

2026-08-30 tokenizer section replaced with the upstream tokenizer.json (weights unchanged): answers to prompts with accented letters/symbols/emoji can change; accuracy figures and any on-device rows were measured on the previous file; the on-device gate has not been re-run.

2026-08-31 chat template fix (metadata-only, weights unchanged): history turns with role 'assistant' are now accepted; single-turn renders, token ids, prefill counts and greedy answers are unchanged, so the card's numbers still describe this file.

measured.source: model card: Performance table (litert-lm benchmark, Apple M4 Max) (card retrieved 2026-09-05)

S4 GPU gate, 205-token benchmark, single run; full delegation (3098 ops across 3 subgraphs); generation gate answered the probe correctly. No same-device CPU control was taken, so this is a GPU speed, not a measured win over CPU.

S7 Android backfill: same-device CPU control - identical binary, prompt file and flags, only --backend differs; 205-token prompt with --benchmark, 2 cold runs (compile/weight caches deleted between runs, device cooled below 42 C before each run); the GPU path does not run for this file on this handset, so this row has no GPU counterpart

known_issues: macOS GPU backend is not usable on litert-lm 0.15.0: with --backend gpu it returns a run of '!' characters instead of a caption; the benchmark still reports 5,583 tok/s prefill / 342 tok/s decode on that unusable path, so no GPU row is quoted. Desktop-runtime observation only.

GPU (Metal) backend: a second image in the same conversation truncates the answer; ask about one image per chat. GPU-delegate-specific, not a model/bundle issue — on the CPU backend multi-image works perfectly (verified); reproduces with other fast_vlm models.
